findings.breaking_input: Manifest lists `.agents/skills/x/SKILL.md`, but `.agents` (or `.agents/skills`) inside the project is a symlink/junction to a directory outside the project. uninstall calls safePath (which per the ADR realpath-checks) but then does `lstatSync(abs)`, `readFileSync(abs)` and `rmSync(abs)` on the unresolved path; if the link is swapped in after safePath's check (or safePath only checks the final component), the rm follows the link and deletes a file outside the project. Also the later `rmdirSync(join(dir,d))` for each ancestor dir in `dirs` is never passed through safePath, so a linked ancestor directory is rmdir'd through the link.
findings.why: Check-then-use on a path with a linked parent; the removal and rmdir calls re-resolve the path rather than using the verified real path.
findings.fix: Use the realpath returned by safePath for lstat/read/rm, and re-verify with lstat of every parent segment immediately before rmdir; skip any ancestor that is a link.
findings.twin_of: (ah) a linked parent hides a scanned directory.

findings.breaking_input: One managed file cannot be removed (locked on Windows) during upgrade. The first manifest write already put the new record without it; then rec2 is rebuilt from `m.files[p]`. For a v2 manifest `m.files[p]` is normalized to a sha string, so `{sha: m.files[p]}` is right, but the second apply() is called with no `backup` option and an empty writes list: if the process dies between the first apply and the second, the record has dropped a path that is still on disk.
findings.why: The record is rewritten before removals land (the very defect (dn) says was fixed); the fix only repairs it after the fact in a second non-atomic write.
findings.fix: Attempt removals first (or compute stuck set before writing), then write the manifest once with the stuck paths retained.
findings.twin_of: (dn) a record rewritten before its removals land.

findings.breaking_input: Two `arc init` runs in the same millisecond and same pid are impossible, but two runs on different pids read the same list, both add their own entry, and both rename: the loser's rename replaces the winner's file. The retry loop only re-reads and checks that its OWN entry is present, so the winner's entry is lost silently when the loser holds (the loser's list did not contain the winner's entry, and the loser's check passes).
findings.why: Read-modify-write with last-rename-wins and a verification that only checks this writer's entry; the other writer's verification may pass first and the other entry is dropped for good.
findings.fix: Take an exclusive lock file (wx) around read-modify-write, or after rename re-read and re-add any entry that was in a previously-read list from another writer.

findings.breaking_input: `~/.arc-private/consumers.json` is a symlink to a path elsewhere (or `~/.arc-private` itself is a link). writeRegistry writes `${file}.pid.ts.tmp` into the dir and renames over the link name, replacing the link with a regular file; a corrupt-file branch `renameSync(cur.path, cur.path + '.bad')` renames the link, not its target.
findings.why: A predictable temp name is created with plain writeFileSync (no `wx` flag), so a pre-planted link at that name is written through; the registry dir is not confined.
findings.fix: Open the temp with flag `wx`, refuse a registry dir or file that is a link, and use a random temp suffix.
findings.twin_of: (as) a predictable temp name is written through.

findings.breaking_input: Registry entry `path` is a case-different spelling or an 8.3 short name of the same Windows directory; also a registered path that is a relative string such as `..\\other` hand-edited into consumers.json. outdatedAll passes `c.path` straight to `outdated()`/`existsSync` with no confinement or absolute check; fold() dedup compares spellings only.
findings.why: Registry data is untrusted input from a file the owner edits; relative paths resolve against the radar's cwd and read manifests from unintended directories, and case-fold applied only on one side of some comparisons produces duplicates.
findings.fix: Require absolute paths on read (isAbsolute), realpath them, and dedupe on the realpath.

findings.breaking_input: `arc init` (no --target) on a project that already has `.arc-install.json` from `--target claude-code` (the old claude-code record lives elsewhere, `.claude/arc-registry.json`). `readManifest` returns `prior.rel !== MANIFEST` and refuses; but a prior single-target codex v1 install is treated as `prior`, and `L.safePath` is applied to the old paths only, while `pre.conflicts` come from preflight against `prior.manifest`: files of the v1 install owned by a different target are overwritten by a new owner without a backup if their sha equals the manifest sha but the owner changes.
findings.why: Ownership changes across a re-init are applied as plain writes; with `--force` absent the conflict logic keys on sha only, so a file moved from codex to skills-only ownership is silently rewritten.
findings.fix: Treat an owner change as an explicit planned op and list it in the plan output; back up when the on-disk sha differs from the manifest sha.

findings.breaking_input: `upgrade --to v0.2.0` run with env `GIT_DIR` unset but `GIT_COMMON_DIR`, `GIT_OBJECT_DIRECTORY`, `GIT_ALTERNATE_OBJECT_DIRECTORIES`, `GIT_NAMESPACE`, or `GIT_CEILING_DIRECTORIES` set in the caller's environment (a git hook context sets GIT_INDEX_FILE and others). Only GIT_DIR and GIT_WORK_TREE are deleted from `env`.
findings.why: An inherited GIT_OBJECT_DIRECTORY redirects the object lookups so read-tree fails or reads from a different store than the one resolved for the verified tag; the verified ref and the used object store differ.
findings.fix: Delete every GIT_* variable except the ones set explicitly (or build env from a minimal allowlist).

findings.breaking_input: Manifest holds `.codex/a.md` and `.Codex/A.md` style paths on a case-insensitive filesystem (Windows/macOS), or two manifest paths that realpath to the same file. The first is judged and removed; the second reports `gone`. More importantly, a managed path whose on-disk entry is a directory junction on Windows is reported by lstat as a directory (`kept (not a file)`), while a symlink to a file reads `isFile() === false` and is kept; but a hardlink to a file outside the project passes `isFile()`, matches the sha, and `rmSync` removes only the link, which is fine, while `--force` with a file whose sha differs removes the project's own copy without any backup.
findings.why: `--force` deletes a modified managed file with no copy kept, unlike upgrade which backs it up; the owner's edits are destroyed.
findings.fix: Back up (as upgrade does) before removing any modified file under --force, or require a separate explicit flag.

findings.breaking_input: Registry has a consumer on a network drive that hangs, or a consumer whose manifest names a huge file set; `outdatedAll` runs `git` via spawnSync with no timeout for every consumer in sequence. Also `spawnSync("bash", ...)` is resolved by PATH: from PowerShell the PATH `bash` is WSL's, so the emit runs inside WSL with a Windows path as argv[1] and fails every week.
findings.why: No per-consumer timeout, so one hung project blocks the whole radar (and the job's budget); and a binary resolved via PATH differs by launching shell (the known HQ-from-PowerShell failure).
findings.fix: Pass a `timeout` to every spawnSync in the radar path and resolve bash from Git for Windows explicitly or invoke arc-event through node.

findings.breaking_input: STAMP is written after a successful emit; if `mkdirSync`/`writeFileSync` of the stamp throws (read-only state dir), the exception is an unhandled rejection inside `main().then(...)` with no catch, so the process exits with the default code and the receipt is emitted again on every daily run.
findings.why: `main().then(c => process.exitCode = c)` has no rejection handler; a throw from outdatedAll (e.g. thrown Refused from a corrupt consumer manifest) escapes as a stack with exit code 1 only by Node default, and nothing is stamped, so the same failure repeats.
findings.fix: Add `.catch` that prints the failure and sets a distinct exit code, and wrap per-consumer errors (already partly done) plus the stamp write.

findings.breaking_input: `Promise.resolve(main(...)).then(c => { process.exitCode = c; })` with a rejected promise (any non-Refused throw inside `lifecycle`/`init`, e.g. a corrupt manifest JSON in readManifest, or EPERM).
findings.why: No catch: Node prints an unhandled rejection and exits 1 with no `RAN arc-<verb>` line, which the tests treat as the proof the command ran, so a crash is indistinguishable from a handled exit 1, and verbs that must exit 2 for bad input exit 1.
findings.fix: Add a catch that prints the error, prints the RAN line, and sets exit code 2.
findings.twin_of: (cc) a render failure that escapes as a stack.

findings.breaking_input: `--root` pointing at a directory whose `package.json` is a directory or unreadable, or CHANGELOG.md using CRLF with a trailing space (`## [0.2.0] - 2026-10-14 `). `readFileSync` throws EISDIR/EACCES from `read()` uncaught; and a heading with trailing whitespace fails the strict regex, reported as a malformed section rather than ignored.
findings.why: existsSync-then-read treats a directory as present; the throw escapes as a stack trace and exit 1/unspecified instead of the documented exit 2.
findings.fix: Wrap read in try/catch returning null, and trimEnd each heading line before matching.
findings.twin_of: (ae) a malformed field read as absent.

findings.breaking_input: `ps -o lstart=` output on a locale that prints the date in another format or with a two-digit day padded differently (e.g. a non-English LC_TIME, or macOS vs procps column width). The regex requires five whitespace-separated tokens ending in a year; any other shape makes every row fail to parse, so `posixProcs()` returns an empty map rather than null.
findings.why: An empty map is read as 'no process alive': reapStale sees `wcmd === null` for a live wrapper and goes on to reap a run still in progress, and the kill-set check `now(pid) === cmd` drops every live child so survivors are not recorded.
findings.fix: Force `LC_ALL=C` on the ps spawn and return null when no row parses.
